name: Can you move a shower drain without moving the whole shower?

mainEntity.name: Can you move a shower drain without moving the whole shower?
mainEntity.text: Can you move a shower drain without moving the whole shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: A shower drain can sometimes be moved without changing the entire shower, but the new drain position has to align with the shower base, slope, and waterproofing system. Minor adjustments are easier when the shower footprint stays close to the original area. If the shower pan is changing shape or size, the drain move often becomes part of a larger rebuild that includes framing, pan construction, and wall waterproofing. On slab floors, the drain relocation can mean cutting concrete and rebuilding the base around the new trap location. On framed floors, access from below may make the work easier, but the system still has to drain correctly and pass inspection. Homeowners should not assume a drain-only move is simple just because the shower walls stay in place. The drain location, tile layout, and waterproofing details all need to be coordinated before any demolition starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but the drain still has to match the new shower pan or waterproofing layout. In many remodels, moving only the drain is possible if the shower footprint changes slightly, but larger changes usually require modifying the full shower base and plumbing rough-in.
